we have developed a novel generic probabilistic channel (GPC) model that can capture a large class of channel models and can be applied to analyze the connectivity of wireless networks.
we derived an exact closed-form formula to calculate the expected number of Isolated Nodes (IN) in a wireless network, and that we proved the asymptotic distribution of IN is Poisson distribution.

the expected number of the isolated nodes in a random network with n nodes is O(n) and the number of the isolated follows a Poisson process with parameter λ = O(n), which is asymptotically equivalent to the number of isolated in a random graph with edge probability p = O(n−1).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the connectivity analysis of wireless networks.
the number of isolated vertices in a random network.
the analysis of the number of isolated wireless nodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probability of connectivity of the wireless network asymptotically equals to 1 minus the expected number of the isolated nodes.
this paper provides an analysis of the number of isolated vertices in a wireless network with a probabilistic channel model.

the number of isolated vertices in a wireless network follows a Poisson Distribution, and the probability of connectivity is asymptotically equivalent to the probability that no nodes in the network are isolated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
